objective: Test whether a train-only input-reconstruction decoder, with or without literal residual AuxK, reduces late fuzzy-feature death without materially degrading language-model validation loss.
comparison_policy: All arms use identical deployed architecture, initialization seed, data stream, token schedule, optimizer, topology, and evaluation. Training-only matrix work is reported rather than equalized because shortening a treatment would confound the auxiliary-objective intervention.

required: finite compilation, training, reconstruction metrics, and validation
unit-row reconstruction decoder invariant after optimization
complete packed training and full-feature sparsity logs
reconstruction throughput at least half the paired parent throughput
AuxK incremental training-time overhead no more than 15 percent versus reconstruction-only

primary: persistent dead-feature fraction on aligned final sparsity captures
mechanism: reconstruction NMSE by layer and step
AuxK NMSE and positive auxiliary fraction by layer and step
dead-group fraction, positive-group rate, and within-group winner entropy

evidence_boundary: This is a paired one-seed mechanism screen on one preemptible v6e-8 topology. It can select or reject the implementation for a later multi-seed ladder, but is not itself a seed-robust quality conclusion.
